title: finding(plugin-detail): `record:alert`'s CTA lookup is a third hand-written by-name resolver beside the one objectui#7182 unified
body:
Found while implementing objectui#7182 (PR #7381). Filed rather than ridden: that card's ruling names two renderers and one function; this is a third site of the same mechanism at arity one, and touching it was outside the dispatched surface.

## What is there

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx` lines 241-249 (on `main` `d53e472`): the optional CTA is resolved from the object's own metadata through the same `useMetadataItem('object', name)` read the other two surfaces use, then looked up by hand — `(objectMeta.actions).find((a) => a.name === ctaName)` — with the read skipped when no CTA is requested. Same mechanism (the object's `actions[]`, keyed on `name`), written out a third time, one element wide.

Re-check commands: `git grep -n "ctaName" -- packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx` (should hit the `find`), and the control `git grep -n "resolveDeclaredActionIds" -- packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` (hits once PR #7381 lands).

## Why it is observation-class and not a defect

A single declared id cannot be mixed, so none of the objectui#7182 divergence reaches this site — an unknown `actionName` resolves to `undefined` and the CTA simply does not render, silently (no warn-once diagnostic, unlike `page:header`'s unresolved-id warning). The point is the same one objectui#5935 makes for the lucide icon resolvers and objectui#7182 made for the two action arrays: the by-name lookup should have one home, and `resolveDeclaredActionIds([ctaName], objectMeta.actions)` is now that home. Routing this site through it would also give the CTA the unresolved-id report the header already has.

Blocked-by: objectui#7182 landing (PR #7381) — the function this would call is introduced there.

Filed unassigned by the objectui#7182 dev seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Attribution written as prose because issue creation strips a footer block.
